However, a purchase shall not be considered a "purchase of a going business" unless the business continues to be operated under the same trade name and at the same location for a period of 12 months subsequent to the date of purchase.
Restaurant means any public place kept, used, maintained, advertised and held out to the public as a place where meals are served and where meals are actually and regularly served, such place being provided with adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining room equipment, air conditioned, having employed therein a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook, and serve suitable food for its guests. At least one meal per day shall be served on at least three days per week, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and period of redecoration, and the serving of such meals shall be the principal business conducted, with the service of alcoholic beverages to be consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto. A restaurant shall provide at least 24 seats for its customers, and shall derive at least 50 percent of its gross revenue from the sale of food prepared on the premises. A restaurant must also have a valid food service establishment permit as required by O.C.G.A. § 26-2-371.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22; Ord. No. 511, § 1, 8-16-22)
172:
This chapter has been enacted in accordance with a plan designed for the purposes, among others, of promoting the health and general welfare of the community; to establish reasonable standards for the regulation and control of the licensing, sale and dispensing of alcoholic beverages, to protect and preserve the schools; to give effect to existing land use; to protect those of minor age in the community; and to preserve reasonable and orderly land use, with reasonable considerations, among others, to the character of the areas and their peculiar suitability for particular uses, the congestion in the roads and streets, and with a general view of promoting desirable living conditions and sustaining the stability of neighborhoods and property value ; to protect against the evils of concentration of outlets for malt beverages and wine in one person or entity or to prevent undesirable persons or entities from controlling the malt beverage and wine industry in the city; and to ensure that only grocery stores are licensed to sell malt beverages and wine at retail in the city as an incidental part of their business and to protect against the evils of beer and wine stores per se; to insure that only restaurants (and not bars per se) are authorized to sell malt beverages and/or wine by the drink; and to provide for the licensing of wholesale dealers and importers with physical locations in the city.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
174:
It shall be lawful to sell malt beverages and wine at retail by the package in the city only when granted a license by the city. Additionally, it shall be lawful to sell malt beverages and wine at retail by the drink only when granted a license by the city.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
175:
All individual retail licensees and/or persons holding a license on behalf of a sole proprietor, a corporation, a limited liability company or a partnership shall meet the following qualifications:
(1) Such person shall be a resident of the United States.
(2) Such person shall be of good moral character and shall not have been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to any felony, any violation of controlled substance laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, in any state of the United States, within the five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(3) Such person shall not have had his license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(4) Such person shall be the owner of the premises, or the holder of a valid written lease thereon, or the person with a primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
176:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or the owner of the premises, or the holder of a valid lease thereon shall be the holder of the license on behalf of a sole proprietorship, and shall possess all of the qualification set forth in section 6-4.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
177:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to he operated on the licensed premises, or the holder of the majority of shares in the corporation shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the corporation, and shall possess all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-4.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
178:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or a general partner, shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the partnership, and shall possess all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-4.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
179:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or, if the LLC entity has a manager, such manager, or if the LLC entity has no manager, a member of the LLC, shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the LLC, and shall possess all the qualifications set forth in section 6-4.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
180:
In the event there is a change in the person holding the license for an entity licensed by the city to sell alcoholic beverages, and said entity timely files with the city manager the information regarding the change as required by subsection 6-13(b), the new person who shall be the "person holding the license on behalf of licensee" shall be given a period of 90 days to meet the qualifications under this chapter before such entity's license is cancelled, suspended, or revoked.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
181:
Any person having an ownership interest in the licensee:
(1) Shall not have been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to any felony, any violation of controlled substances laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs in any state of the United States within the five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(2) Shall not have had an ownership interest of 25 percent or greater in any entity which has had its license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
182:
(a) General qualifications. A package licensee must prove that it is a grocery store.
(b) Making application. The licensee must prove that it has experienced grocery sales of at least $25,000.00 during the three months immediately preceding the filing of the application at the licensed premises or the premises to be licensed, excluding the sale of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). Such proof shall be made by providing copies of sales tax returns and cancelled checks or other evidence of payment of sales tax together with an affidavit from the licensee or the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the licensee, swearing or affirming under oath that the premises has experienced grocery sales of at least $25,000.00 excluding the sale of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). The mayor and council may, in their discretion, require an audited financial statement by a certified public accountant providing for a detailed analysis of sales, categorizing sales of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes, and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). The cost of such audited financial statement shall be borne by the licensee.
(c) Checks and audits after issuance. The licensee is subject to subsequent checks and audits of its books and records after issuance of the license by the city clerk or his or her designated agent during regular business hours, the cost of which shall be borne by the city. The licensee shall maintain grocery sales of at least $50,000.00, excluding the sale of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items), during the 12-month period immediately preceding such licensee's application for renewal. If the license has been issued for a period of less than 12 months immediately preceding the filing of the application for renewal by such licensee, the $50,000.00 grocery sales requirement shall be prorated for the period in which such licensee has held a license immediately preceding the filing of the application for renewal.
(d) Checks and audits prior to renewal. The licensee must prove that it has experienced grocery sales of at least $50,000.00 for the period immediately preceding the filing of the application as set forth in subsection (c) above. Such proof shall be made by providing copies of sales tax returns and cancelled checks or other evidence of payment of sales tax together with an affidavit from the licensee or the person who holds the license on behalf of the licensee, swearing or affirming under oath that the premises has experienced grocery sales of at least $50,000.00 during the 12-month period immediately preceding such licensee's application for renewal (or in an amount prorated for the period in which such licensee has held a license immediately preceding the filing of the application for renewal) excluding the sale of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). The mayor and council may, in its discretion, and upon reasonable suspicion that the licensee has not experienced the requisite grocery sales, require an audited financial statement by a certified public accountant, providing for a detailed analysis of sales, categorizing gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes, and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items), the cost of which shall be borne by the licensee.
(e) Exceptions, chain grocery stores; purchase of going business.
(1) Chain grocery stores. The provision of this section requiring an applicant to prove grocery sales of at least $25,000.00 during the three months immediately preceding the filing of the application shall not, at the option of any chain grocery store applicant, apply to chain grocery stores. If such applicant's sales do not equal or exceed $250,000.00 for the first three months of operation subsequent to the issuance of a malt beverage and wine license, such license shall be revoked and the applicant must reapply for a malt beverage and wine license, which application shall not be considered for a period of three months subsequent to revocation under this section. The holder of the license on behalf of the applicant must furnish the city clerk sales tax returns and cancelled checks or other evidence of payment of sales tax for its first three months of operation within 30 days of the end of the three-month period in order to demonstrate requisite grocery sales, together with an affidavit from the person holding a license on behalf of the licensee that the subject chain grocery store has experienced grocery sales of at least $250,000.00 during the three-month period. Additionally, the mayor and council may, in its discretion, require an audited financial statement providing for a detailed analysis of sales, categorizing sales of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). The cost of such audited financial statement shall be borne by the licensee.
(2) Purchase of going business. The provision of this section requiring an applicant to prove grocery sales of at least $25,000.00 during the three months immediately preceding the filing of the application shall not, at the option of the purchaser of a going business holding a valid malt beverage and wine license in the city, apply to such applicant. If such applicant's sales do not equal or exceed $25,000.00 for the first three months of operation subsequent to the issuance of a malt beverage and wine license, such license shall be revoked and the applicant must reapply for a malt beverage and wine license, which application shall not be considered for a period of three months subsequent to revocation under this section. The holder of the license on behalf of the applicant must furnish the city clerk sales tax returns and cancelled checks or other evidence of payments of sales tax for its first three months of operation within 30 days of the end of the three-month period in order. to demonstrate requisite grocery sales, together with an affidavit from the person holding a license on behalf of the licensee that the subject grocery store has experienced grocery sales of at least $25,000.00 during the three-month period. Additionally, the mayor and council may, in its discretion, require an audited financial statement providing for a detailed analysis of sales, categorizing sales of gasoline, motor oil, cigarettes and prepared food cooked or heated on the licensed premises (including, but not limited to, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizza, fried chicken, sandwiches and bakery items). The cost of such audited financial statement shall be borne by the licensee.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
183:
(a) General qualifications. A pouring licensee must prove that it is a restaurant.
(b) Making application. The licensee must prove that it meets or shall meet before commencing business the definition of a restaurant as provided in this chapter, except for the percentage of food sales, which must be subsequently proven as hereinafter set forth.
(c) Proof of food sales after issuance.
(1) Initial proof. The licensee must prove that at least 50 percent of its gross revenue for the first three months that it began selling beer and/or wine by the drink was derived from the sale of food prepared on the licensed premises, or such license shall be immediately revoked. Such proof as hereinafter set forth shall be provided to the city clerk within four months of the issuance of the license. Such proof shall be made by providing copies of sales tax returns, cancelled checks or other evidence of payment of sales tax; records of the licensee providing proof of the dollar amount from sales of alcoholic beverages; and an affidavit from the licensee or the person who holds the license on behalf of the licensee, swearing or affirming on oath that 50 percent of the gross revenue for the first three months that the licensee began selling alcoholic beverages by the drink was derived from the sale of food prepared on the licensed premises. The mayor and council may, in its discretion, require an audited financial statement by a certified public accountant providing for a detailed analysis of the sources of the gross revenue. The cost of such audited financial statement shall be borne by the licensee.
(2) Checks and audits after issuance. The licensee is subject to subsequent checks and audits of its books and records after issuance of the license by the city clerk or his designated agent during regular business hours, the cost of which shall be borne by the city.
(3) Checks and audits prior to renewal. The licensee must prove that at least 50 percent of its gross revenue is derived from food prepared on the licensed premises during the 12 months immediately preceding such licensee's application for renewal (or, if licensed for less than 12 months, for the period that the license has been held). The mayor and council may, in its discretion, and upon reasonable suspicion that the licensee has not met the requisite food sales for such period, require an audited financial statement by a certified public accountant, providing for a detailed analysis of the sources of gross revenue. The cost of such audited financial statement shall be borne by the licensee.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
184:
No license to sell malt beverages and wine shall be granted at a location within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds, or college campus. As used in this article the term "school building" shall apply only to state, county, city, or church school buildings and to such buildings at such other schools in which are taught subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of this state and which are public schools or private schools as defined in O.C.G.A. § 20-2-690(b). The 100-yard distance shall be measured along the most direct legal route of travel on the ground and from building to building at any part thereof. However, this provision shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to the adoption of the ordinance from which this section derives, nor at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of malt beverages and wine was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding application for a malt beverage and wine license. Provided, however, the within and foregoing 100-yard distance requirement shall be reduced to 50 feet with respect to locations within the Sylvania Downtown Central Business District as shown, for purposes of this chapter, on the map attached to Ord. No. 508, as exhibit "A", for which a pouring license for either malt beverages, wine, or both, has been issued and is in effect.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
185:
(a) All applications for licenses under this article shall be made on forms furnished the applicant by the city clerk and shall indicate the following:
(1) The names and addresses of all persons having an ownership interest in the business applying for the license to sell malt beverages and wine, together with the interest each person or any member of his immediate family has in any other business license to sell malt beverages and wine in the city.
(2) The ownership of the land and building where the business is to be operated, together with a copy or copies of deeds to and leases thereon.
(3) Whether the licensee, the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the licensee, or any person having an ownership interest in the licensee, has been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to any felony, any violation of controlled substances laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, in any state of the United States within the five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(4) Whether the licensee, the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the licensee or any person having an ownership interest in the licensee has had his license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(5) The name of the licensee (business entity), and the name, address and telephone number of the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the business entity, if different.
(6) A set of fingerprints of persons having an ownership interest in the licensee as well as the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee, which fingerprints must be processed through the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and the National Crime Information Center (NCIC).
(7) Photographs of the person managing the business, together persons with an ownership interest primarily responsible for with photograph is of all in the business.
(8) Any other information called for by the mayor and council.
(b) Any change in any relationship declared in the application with regard to persons interested in the ownership of the business, or in the relationship between the person holding the license on behalf of the business and the business itself, must be filed with the city manager when the change is made. The failure to so file within a period of 30 days after the change is made shall be grounds for cancellation, revocation or suspension of the license by the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
186:
A fee in the amount of $130.00 shall be paid to the city at the time of the filing of the application under this article to defray costs and expenses in connection with the filing of the application and the investigation of the applicant and of the facts contained in the application.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
187:
All applications for licenses shall be acted upon by the mayor and council after a public hearing and advertisement thereof in at least two consecutive issues of the legal organ of the city, which notice shall contain a particular description of the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and the name of the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the applicant, if different, and if a partnership, the names of all general and limited partners, and if a corporation or limited liability company, the names of the person who shall have primary responsibility for managing the business together with the names of the owners having at least 25 percent of the shares of stock each in such corporation, together with the names of the officers and board of directors, and if a limited liability company, the names of the owners of at least 25 percent interests each in such limited liability company. The public hearing shall be held not sooner than ten days nor more than 20 days subsequent to the date of the first advertisement.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
188:
When the malt beverage and/or wine license has been approved by the mayor and council and the applicant has deposited with the city manager the required application fee, the required alcohol license tax, the required occupation tax, and any other fees and taxes due the city by the applicant, the applicable license or licenses will be issued. The license, when issued, shall authorize the licensee to conduct the retail sale of either malt beverages, wine, or both.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
189:
Licenses issued under this article shall have a term beginning January 1 of the year of issuance and shall terminate on December 31 of the year of issuance at midnight. Licenses issued after January 1 of any given year shall be valid only through December 31 of that year at midnight, and such licensee shall pay all fees and taxes owed for a full year. In the event of revocation, surrender or suspension of the license prior to the expiration of the term, the holder shall not be entitled to receive any refund of any fees or taxes whatsoever.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
190:
(a) Generally. Licenses under this article shall not be transferable except as provided in this section.
(b) Sole proprietor. If the holder of this license is the sole proprietor of the business, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to the personal representative of his estate or to a member of his immediate family upon the sole proprietor's death, provided that such person meets all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-5. If the holder of the license on behalf of the sole proprietor is not the owner of the business, but rather is the person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises, and such person ceases to be the person with such primary responsibility, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to a person meeting all qualifications set forth in section 6-5.
(c) Corporations. If the holder of the license on behalf of a corporation ceases to be either the person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises, or the holder of the majority of shares in the corporation, subsequent to the issuance of the license, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to a person meeting all qualifications set forth in section 6-6.
(d) Partnerships. If the holder of the license on behalf of a partnership ceases to be either the person having primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises, or a general partner in the business, subsequent to the issuance of the license, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to a person meeting all qualifications set forth in section 6-7.
(e) Limited liability companies. If the holder of the license on behalf of a limited liability company ceases to be either the person having primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises, or the manager or a member of the LLC, subsequent to the issuance of the license, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to a person meeting all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-8.
(f) Sale of licensed premises. No license shall be transferred from one business entity to another upon the sale or lease of the licensed premises. However, this subsection shall not apply to a sole proprietor or to a partnership which continues its business on the licensed premises in the form of a corporation or limited liability company after issuance of the license provided that the sole proprietor remains the owner of 100 percent of the shares/interests in the corporation or limited liability company, or in the case of a partnership, as long as the same partners remain the owner of 100 percent of the shares/interests in the corporation or limited liability company.
Provided further, if there is a transfer in ownership of the licensee, but the manager for a new applicant remains the same as the former licensee, and that manager was the holder of the license on behalf of the former licensee, and shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the new applicant, the license may, in the discretion of the mayor and council, be transferred to the new applicant for a period of 90 days commencing with the date of the sale or transfer in ownership, in order for the new applicant to have the time needed to complete the application process for a license for the new applicant.
(g) Transfer of location. The holder of a valid license issued as provided in this chapter may request that the license be transferred from the licensed premises to a new location of the licensed business, which license may be transferred upon approval by the mayor and council.
191:
(a) Renewal process. All holders of retail malt beverage and wine licenses in the city shall apply for renewal thereof for the subsequent year between November 1 of the current year for which the licensee holds a valid license and November 30 of such year. In the application for renewal, the licensee shall state any changes in information that was provided on the licensee's original application to the city for a malt beverage and/or wine license. A package licensee shall also provide proof of grocery sales as provided for in subsection 6-10(d). A pouring licensee shall also provide proof of sales of prepared foods on the licensed premises as provided for in subsection 6-11(c)(3). All malt beverage and wine licenses shall be deemed automatically renewed for the subsequent year unless the mayor and council deny renewal thereof on or before December 31 of the current year. There shall be no application fee for renewal of an existing license. If an application for renewal is not filed within the requisite time limits set forth herein, such licensee shall begin anew the application process as though the licensee had never held a malt beverage and/or wine license in the city. All applications for renewal shall be accompanied by payment of the malt beverage and/or wine license tax, which amount shall be returned if renewal of such license is denied.
(b) Change in information. In the event there has been a change in any person having an ownership interest in the licensee, or in the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee, a set of fingerprints of such new person or persons shall be made and processed through the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and the National Crime Information Center (NCIC). If any such person has been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to any felony, any violation of controlled substances laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting the operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, in any state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application for, renewal, said license shall not be renewed, or if already renewed, shall be revoked.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
192:
No holder of a retail license which authorizes the sale of malt beverages and/or wine by the package in the city, nor any agents or employees of the licensee, shall knowingly and intentionally allow or permit the breaking of any package or packages containing alcoholic beverages on the premises where sold or allow or permit the drinking of the contents of such package or packages on the premises where sold.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
194:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or for any person to purchase malt beverages or wine in the city unless the purchaser exhibits proper identification to the seller. For purposes of this chapter, the term "proper identification" means any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph, or both, and giving such person's date of birth and includes without being limited to a passport, military identification card or driver's license. "Proper identification" shall not include a birth certificate. This section applies to all persona regardless of age, and regardless of whether such person appears to be of proper and lawful age to purchase malt beverages or wine.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
195:
Properly licensed wholesale dealers are authorized to make sales or deliveries with respect to retailers, only to retailers properly licensed under this chapter for the operation of establishments in the city. Deliveries shall be made in a conveyance owned, leased and operated by a wholesaler licensed under this chapter, and hie license or permit shall at all times when deliveries are made in the city be in the conveyance making these deliveries and shall be subject all times to inspection by all duly authorized authorities of the city. Under no circumstances shall any wholesale dealer sell or deliver any distilled spirits to any establishment in the incorporated areas of the city.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
196:
The retail dealers in malt beverages and wine, licensed under this chapter shall not buy or accept deliveries of malt beverages or wine from wholesalers or other persons offering them for sale except from wholesalers duly authorized under this chapter. These retailers shall not accept delivery of malt beverages or wine except directly to the premises for which their license and permit was issued, and by no other means than a conveyance owned or leased and operated by a wholesaler properly licensed to make deliveries of malt beverages and wine in the city.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
197:
All licensed premises shall be referred the malt beverages and wine in the possession of a retailer shall be stored and sold in and upon the for which the license was issued, which premises described in the application for licenses hereinabove to, and at no other place.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
198:
Except as hereinafter set forth in this section, it shall be unlawful for any person to sell, give away or offer for sale, or in any other manner dispense or deliver any malt beverage or wine within the corporate limits of the city during the hours of 12:00 midnight on each Saturday and until 7:00 a.m. on each Monday. Provided, however, package licensees are authorized to sell and offer for sale malt beverages and wine by the package within the corporate limits of the city on Sundays between the hours of 12:30 p.m. and 11:30 p.m.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
199:
It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or consume any malt beverage or wine on or upon the public streets, roads or alleys in the city, or any public park or playground, or on any other public property.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
200:
Persons obtaining retail licenses under this article for the sale of malt beverages and wine by the package shall not allow the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises of their respective places of business.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
201:
It is prohibited for any person to bring in his own malt beverage or wine in any restaurant in the city.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
202:
(a) No package licensee under this article shall advertise the sale of malt beverages or wine at his establishment by any sign or similar device on the exterior of the building in which his business is located, or at any other exterior location on the lot or parcel of land on which his building is located, or on any other tract or parcel of land with n the city limits. Within the building in which his business is located, such licensee may display any number of signs, but such signs shall not be so prominently visible from outside such building as to defeat the intent of the restriction on exterior advertisement.
(b) Signs which are located in a window of a building in which a package licensee's business is located and all lighted signs, wherever located, shall be considered to be so prominently visible from outside such building as to defeat the intent of the restriction on exterior advertising.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
203:
There shall be no prohibition against the sale and purchase of malt beverages or wine on election days.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
204:
(a) Package license. There shall be a license tax levied on all package licensees in the amount of $1,000.00 per year, which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license.
(b) Pouring license.
(1) Beer pouring license. There shall be a license tax levied on all pouring licensees for malt beverages only in the amount of $250.00 per year, which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license.
(2) Wine pouring license. There shall be a license tax levied on all pouring licensees for wine only in the amount of $250.00 per year which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license.
(3) Combined beer and wine pouring license. There shall be a license tax levied on all pouring licensees for beer and wine in the amount of $500.00 per year, which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license.
(c) Refund of license tax. If the license is not issued in connection with such application, the license tax shall be returned.
(d) Renewal. In the case of renewal, the tax shall be due and payable at the time application is made for renewal, which amount shall be returned if renewal is denied by the mayor and council.
(e) Possible pro-ration. The Sylvania City Council in its discretion, may pro-rate the license tax for that portion of a year in which the issuance of a new or renewed license is delayed due to any mistake, error, or unreasonable delay caused by the city, the State of Georgia, or the United States, but only where such mistake, error, or unreasonable delay is not caused by or contributed to by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
205:
There is hereby imposed upon each licensed wholesale dealer making deliveries to retail licensees located within the city an excise tax, in addition to the excise taxes levied by the state, as follows:
(1) Malt beverages.
a. Where malt beverages, commonly known as tap or draft beer, are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons.

206:

(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
207:
No natural person, partnership, limited partnership, corporation or other entity shall hold more than two retail malt beverage and wine licenses in the city; nor shall any such person or entity possess a 25 percent or greater ownership interest in more than two holders of retail malt beverage and wine licenses in the city.

Wholesale dealers with one or more physical business locations outside of the city, who possess required licenses from the State of Georgia, are not required to obtain a license from the city, and are allowed to dis tribute alcoholic beverages within the city provided that such wholesale dealers otherwise comply with federal, state and local law and regulations.

(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
210:
All individual licensees and/or persons holding a license on behalf of a sole proprietor, a corporation, an LLC, or a partnership shall meet the following qualifications:
(1) Such person shall be a resident of the United States.

(3) Such person shall not have had his license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(4) Such person shall be the owner of the premises, or the holder of a valid written lease thereon, or the person with a primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the premises.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
211:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or the owner of the premises, or the holder of a valid lease thereon shall be the holder of the license on behalf of a sole proprietorship, and shall possess all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-31.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
212:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or the holder of the majority of shares in the corporation shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the corporation, and shall possess all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-37.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
213:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to be operated on the licensed premises, or, if the LLC entity has a manager, such manager, or if the LLC entity has no manager, a member of the LLC, shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the LLC, and shall possess all the qualifications set forth in section 6-37.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
214:
The person having the primary responsibility for managing the business to he operated on the licensed premises, or a general partner, shall be the holder of the license on behalf of the partnership, and shall possess all of the qualifications set forth in section 6-37.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
215:
Any person having an ownership interest in the licensee:
(1) Shall not have been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to any felony, any violation of controlled substances laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs in any state of the United States within the five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(2) Shall not have had an ownership interest of 25 percent or greater in any entity which has had its license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
216:
(a) All applications for licenses under this article shall be made on forms furnished the applicant by the city clerk and shall indicate the following:
(1) The names and addresses of all persons having an ownership interest in the business applying for the license to sell alcoholic beverages, together with the interest each person or any member of his immediate family has in any other business license to sell alcoholic beverages in the city.

(4) Whether the licensee, the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the licensee or any person having an ownership interest in the licensee has had his license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind revoked for cause by any city, county or state of the United States within five years immediately preceding the filing of the application.

(6) A set of fingerprints of persons having an ownership interest in the licensee as well as the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee, which fingerprints must be processed through the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and the National Crime Information Center (NCIC).

(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
217:
A fee in the amount of $130.00 shall be paid to the city at the time of the filing of the application under this article to defray costs and expenses in connection with the filing of the application and the investigation of the applicant and of the facts contained in the application.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
218:
All applications for licenses shall be acted upon by the mayor and council after a public hearing and advertisement thereof in at least two consecutive issues of the legal organ of the city, which notice shall contain a particular description of the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and the name of the person who shall hold the license on behalf of the applicant, if different, and if a partnership, the names of all general and limited partners, and if a corporation or limited liability company, the names of the person who shall have primary responsibility for managing the business together with the names of the owners having at least 25 percent of the shares of stock each in such corporation, together with the names of the officers and board of directors, and if a limited liability company, the names of the owners of at least 25 percent interests each in such limited liability company. The public hearing shall be held not sooner than ten days nor more than 20 days subsequent to the date of the first advertisement.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
219:
When the wholesaler and/or importer license has been approved by the mayor and council and the applicant has deposited with the city manager the required application fee, the applicable license tax, the applicable occupation tax, and any other fees and taxes due the city by the applicant, a license will be issued. A wholesale license shall authorize a wholesale dealer to conduct the wholesale sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages, and an importer license shall authorize the importer to engage in the importation of alcoholic beverages from another country, and sell the same to another importer, broker or wholesaler.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
220:
Licenses issued under this article shall have a term beginning January 1 of the year of issuance and shall terminate on December 31 of the year of issuance at midnight. Licenses issued after January 1 of any given year shall be valid only through December 31 of that year at midnight, and such licensee shall pay all fees and taxes owed for a full year. In the event of revocation, surrender or suspension of the license prior to the expiration of the term, the holder shall not be entitled to receive any refund of any fees or taxes whatsoever.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
221:
(a) In general. There shall be a license tax levied on all wholesale dealers of alcoholic beverages having a physical business location within the incorporated areas of the city and upon all importers of alcoholic beverages having a physical business location within the incorporated areas of the city. The amount of the wholesale license tax shall be $1,000.00 per year, which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license. The amount of the importer license tax shall be $1,000.00 per year, which tax shall be due and payable upon the filing of the application for the license.
(b) Refund of license tax. If the license is not issued in connection with such application, the license tax shall be returned.
(c) Renewal. In the case of renewal, the tax shall be due and payable at the time application is made for renewal, whi.ch amount shall be returned if renewal is denied by the mayor and council.
(d) Possible pro-ration. The Sylvania City Council in its discretion, may pro-rate the license tax for that portion of a year in which the issuance of a new or renewed license is delayed due to any mistake, error, or unreasonable delay caused by the city, the State of Georgia, or the United States, but only where such mistake, error, or unreasonable delay is not caused by or contributed to by the applicant.
(e) Transferability of licenses. Wholesaler and importer licenses shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
223:
(a) Grounds. The mayor and council may suspend, revoke or deny renewal of any alcoholic beverage license issued under this chapter for due cause. For purposes of this section, due cause is defined as follows:
(1) The conviction of or a plea of nolo contendere by the licensee or any employee or agent of the licensee to a violation of any federal, state, county or municipal law or ordinance relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages, which violation occurred on the licensed premises.
(2) The conviction of or a plea of nolo contendere by any person having an ownership interest in the business located on the licensed premises to any felony, any violation of controlled substances laws, any violation of law regulating the sale of alcoholic beverages, or any violation of law prohibiting operation of a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs in any state of the United States subsequent to the date of issuance of the license.
(3) The revocation for cause by any city, county or state of the United States subsequent to the date of the issuance of the license with respect to an entity that a person having an ownership interest in the business located on the licensed premises as defined herein held an ownership interest in any such entity equaling or exceeding 25 percent.
(4) The failure to provide any change in information set forth in the licensee's original or renewal application for a malt beverage and wine license within 30 days after the date of such change.
(b) Hearing.
(1) Probable cause suspension by mayor. The mayor may, upon probable cause that there is due cause to suspend or revoke a malt beverage and wine license, immediately suspend any license issued under this chapter after an informal hearing with the licensee or the holder of the license on behalf of the licensee. Such hearing shall be held at City Hall between 8:30 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. on any day, Sunday through Saturday, upon two hours' notice, verbal or written, by the Sylvania City Council or its designated agent, to the licensee or the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee. If the licensee or the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee fails to appear at the hearing, or if neither can be notified after reasonable effort, the mayor may, in his discretion, suspend any such license without hearing.
(2) Hearing before council. A hearing before the full mayor and council shall then be held after written notice to such licensee, or the person holding such license on behalf of the licensee, not sooner than two days nor later than ten days subsequent to the date of suspension. Such licensee shall be given at least two days' written notice of the hearing. All decisions of the mayor and council regarding the suspension or revocation of licenses issued under this chapter shall be in writing and the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee.
(c) Notice requirements where no probable cause suspension. In all other cases where there is no probable cause suspension by the Sylvania City Council, a licensee against whom suspension or revocation proceedings are being commenced shall be given at least five days' notice of a hearing before the mayor and council, which notice shall be in writing, and shall be mailed or delivered to such licensee or the person holding such license on behalf of the licensee. All decisions of the mayor and council regarding the suspension or revocation of licenses issued hereunder shall be in writing and the reasons therefore stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
224:
(a) Grounds. The mayor and council may suspend, revoke or deny renewal of any license issued under this chapter for a violation by the licensee or by any employee or agent of the licensee of any provision of this ordinance relating to the licensing and sale of alcoholic beverages, or any amendment thereto, or any provisions of Georgia law relating to the licensing and sale of alcoholic beverages, or any amendment thereto. It shall not be a prerequisite to proceeding under this provision that the licensee or any employee or agent of the licensee be convicted or plead nolo contendere in a court of law to such violation.
(b) Hearing.
(1) Probable cause suspension by mayor. The mayor, upon probable cause that a violation of this chapter has occurred, or that there has been a violation of Georgia law relating to the licensing and sale of alcoholic beverages, immediately suspend any license issued under this chapter after an informal hearing with the licensee or the holder of the license on behalf of the licensee. Such hearing shall be held at City Hall between 8:30 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. on any day, Sunday through Saturday, upon two hours' notice, verbal or written, by the mayor or his designated agent, to the licensee or the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee. If the licensee or the person holding the license on behalf of the licensee fails to appear at the hearing, or if neither can be notified after reasonable effort, the mayor may, in his discretion, suspend any such license without hearing.

A hearing before the full mayor and council shall then ba held after written notice to such licensee, or the person holding such license on behalf of the licensee, not sooner than two days nor later than ten days subsequent to the date of suspension. Such licensee shall be given at least two days' written notice of the hearing. All decisions of the mayor and council regarding the suspension or revocation of licenses issued under this chapter shall be in writing and the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee.
(c) Notice requirements where no probable cause suspension. In all other cases where there is no probable cause suspension by the mayor, a licensee against whom suspension or revocation proceedings are being commenced shall be given at least five days' notice of a hearing before the mayor and council, which notice shall be in writing, and shall be mailed or delivered to such licensee or the person holding such license on behalf of the licensee. All decisions of the mayor and council regarding the suspension or revocation of licenses issued hereunder shall be in writing and the reasons therefore stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
225:
At all hearings before the full council on the issue of suspension, revocation, or the denial of the renewal of any malt beverage and wine license, the licensee shall be afforded an opportunity to present evidence and to cross-examine opposing witnesses. Strict rules of evidence shall not apply. A majority vote of the council members present shall carry any motion. The mayor shall vote only in the case of a tie.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
226:
If a majority of the council present at the hearing finds by a preponderance of the evidence that there are grounds for revoking or suspending a license, revocation of such license is authorized. The mayor and council, may, in its discretion, upon consideration of mitigating factors, impose a lesser penalty of suspension for a specific period of time.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
227:
In cases of sales of malt beverages or wine to persons under the legal drinking age in violation of state law and/or this chapter, the following minimum suspension periods shall apply for any given calendar year:
(1) First violation (during current calendar year): 15 days.
(2) Second violation (during current calendar year): 30 days.
(3) Third violation (during current calendar year): Revocation.
In determining the number of violations under this subsection, only violations which occur on or after January 1, 2001, shall be considered. Nothing contained herein shall preclude the mayor and council from completely revoking a license or from suspending any license for a period of time in addition to the minimum periods set forth in this subsection.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)
228:
Any violation of the provisions of this chapter shall be punishable as provided in section 1-12 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Sylvania.
(Ord. No. 508, 3-1-22)

This chapter shall become effective upon adoption.

236:

237:

(Ord. No. 511, § 2, 8-16-22)
238:
Any license issued to any licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall automatically expire December 31 of the year of its issuance.
Renewal: In the case of renewal, the license tax shall be due and payable at the time application is made for renewal, which amount shall be returned if renewal is denied.
(Ord. No. 511, § 2, 8-16-22)
239:
This chapter shall become effective upon adoption of the ordinance codified herein.
(Ord. No. 511, § 2, 8-16-22)
240:
In the event any part or parts of the ordinance codified in this chapter are determined by any court of competent jurisdiction to be unconstitutional or unlawful, each and every offending part shall be deemed stricken herefrom, and the remaining part or parts of the ordinance shall remain fully effective and enforceable, and shall be construed to carry out the purposes and intents of the ordinance.

No person shall put out or cause to be put out any poison within the city for the killing of any dog or other domestic animal.

(Code 1976, § 10-5002)

(a) No owner or other person shall maintain or harbor within the limits of the city a manifestly vicious dog or other animal unless it is securely, but humanely, confined or restrained in such manner as to prevent this dog or other animal from attacking or biting a person or another animal.
(b) It shall be prima facie evidence of viciousness if a dog or other animal, without provocation, fiercely attacks or bites persons or animals not on the owner's premises.
(Code 1976, § 10-5003)

(a) No person shall bury the carcass of any dead animal other than household pets anywhere inside the city limits.

(Code 1976, § 10-5004)
246:
(a) The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is hereby designated as a bird sanctuary.
(b) It shall be unlawful to trap, hunt, shoot or attempt to shoot or molest in any manner any bird or wildfowl or to rob bird nests or wildfowl nests. However, if starlings or similar birds are found to be congregating in such numbers in a particular locality that they constitute a nuisance or menace to health or property in the opinion of the proper health authorities of the city, the health authorities shall meet with representatives of the Audubon Society, Bird Club, Garden Club or Humane Society, or as many of the clubs as are to be found in the city, after having given the clubs at least three days' actual notice of the time and place of the meeting to the representative of the clubs.

No person shall keep a dog or cat that is three months old or older unless the person has had the dog or cat inoculated for rabies.

All dogs or cats inoculated as provided in section 10-6 shall have attached to or affixed about their necks a collar, with a tag attached thereto, stating the date of the inoculation.
(Code 1976, § 10-5012)
249:
No owner or keeper of any dog or cat shall allow it to run at large upon the streets of the city.

(a) Any dog or cat running at large shall be caught by the police department and placed in a compound for three days.
(b) The owners of these dogs or cats may appear within the three days' time and redeem the dogs or cats by paying the required amount per day for board.
(c) If the dog or cat is not called for within a period of three days, the police department may destroy the dog or cat in a sound, painless manner.
(d) No dog or cat shall be released unless proof of inoculation for rabies is furnished by the owner.
(e) The owner of any impounded dog or cat is hereby required to pay the sum of $1.75 per day while his dog or cat is impounded and the additional sum as charged by the person in charge of the pound for the dog's or cat's maintenance. These sums are to be paid to the city clerk.

(a) Definitions. The following words, terms, or phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section.
(1) Applicant means any person seeking to install a pre-owned manufactured home in the city limits of the City of Sylvania.
(2) Building inspector means the person appointed, employed, or otherwise designated as the director of planning, permits and inspections; the municipal building official or any of his or her assistants or designees;
(3) Certificate of occupancy means a document issued by the building inspector certifying that a pre-owned manufactured home is in compliance with applicable requirements set forth by this section, and indicating it to be in a condition suitable for residential occupancy.
(4) Guarantee of condition bond means a surety bond to guarantee that the affidavit and photographs required by paragraphs a. and b. of subsection (1) of subsection (c) of this section reasonably portray or represents the existing condition of the pre-owned manufactured home proposed for relocation. In lieu of the bond, a cash deposit may be deposited with the city.
(5) Install means to construct a foundation system and to place or erect a manufactured home on such foundation system. Such term includes, without limitation, supporting, blocking, leveling, securing, or anchoring such manufactured home and connecting multiple or expandable sections of such manufactured home.
(6) Jurisdiction means the areas within the city limits of the City of Sylvania, Georgia.
(7) Manufactured home means a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein; except that such term shall include any structure which meets all the requirements of this paragraph except the size requirements and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the secretary of housing and urban development and complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 U. S. C. Section 5401, et seq.
(8) Pre-owned manufactured home means any manufactured home that has been previously used as a residential dwelling and has been titled.
(b) Conditions. All pre-owned manufactured homes located in the jurisdiction shall bear a label certifying it was constructed in compliance with the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 U. S. C. Section 5401, et seq. (the HUD Code) and shall be installed in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 8-2-160 et seq.
(c) Permitting, inspection, certificate of occupancy and fees. A permit shall be required to locate a pre-owned manufactured home in the jurisdiction.
(1) Permit. To obtain a permit, applicants shall provide to the building inspector:
a. An affidavit signed by the applicant that the pre-owned manufactured home meets health and safety standards required by this Act;
b. Photographs of the interior and exterior of the pre-owned manufactured home providing evidence that home meets the minimum health and safety standards of subsection (d) of this section;
c. A $1,000.00 refundable guarantee of condition bond or $1,000.00 refundable cash deposit; and
d. The permit and inspection fee required by subsection (c)(4) of this section.
(2) Inspection. Upon receipt of a permit, applicants may relocate the manufactured home on a residential site for the purposes of inspection. Applicant shall arrange for an inspection to be held once the installation of the manufactured home is complete.
(3) Certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy shall be issued to the applicant at such time that the building inspector certifies that the requirements of this section have been met.
(4) Fee. A permit and inspection fee of $75.00 shall be charged to the applicant to cover the cost to the city to process the permit application and inspect the pre-owned manufactured home. Such fee shall cover the initial inspection and one follow-up inspection. The applicant shall be charged $25.00 for each additional follow-up inspection that may be necessary.
(5) Alternative inspection. At the request of the Applicant, the building inspector may, at his or her discretion, inspect a pre-owned manufactured home prior to its being relocated if the home is then located at another site within the city.
(d) Minimum health and safety standards. All pre-owned manufactured home shall comply with the following before being issued a certificate of occupancy by the building inspector:
(1) HUD Code. Every pre-owned manufactured home located in the jurisdiction shall be in compliance with the Federal Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act, 42 U. S. c. 5401-5445 (the HUD Code) and shall not have been altered in such a way that the home no longer meets the HUD Code.
(2) Interior condition. Every floor, interior wall, and ceiling of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in sound condition. Doors and windows shall be operable, watertight and in good working condition. The floor system shall be in sound condition and free of warping, holes, water damage, or deterioration.
(3) Exterior condition. The exterior of all pre-owned manufactured homes shall be free of loose or rotting boards or timbers and any other conditions that might admit rain or moisture to the interior portions of the walls or to occupied spaces. The exterior siding shall be free of rot and rust. Roofs shall be structurally sound and have no obvious defects that might admit rain or cause moisture to collect on the interior portion of the home.
(4) Sanitary facilities. Every plumbing fixture, water, and waste pipe of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in a sanitary working condition when properly connected, and shall be free from leaks and obstructions. Each home shall contain a kitchen sink. Each bathroom shall contain a lavatory and water closet. At least one bathroom shall contain a tub and/or shower facilities. Each of these fixtures shall be checks upon being connected to ensure they are in good working condition.
(5) Heating systems. Heating shall be safe and in working condition. Un-vented heaters shall be prohibited.
(6) Electrical systems. Switches, receptacles, fixtures, etc. shall be properly installed and wired and shall be in working condition. Distribution panels shall be in compliance with the approved listing, complete with required breakers, with all unused openings covered with solid covers approved and listed for that purpose. The home shall be subject to an electrical continuity test to assure that all metallic parts are properly bonded. Each pre-owned manufactured home shall contain a water heater in safe and working order.
(7) Hot water supply. Each home shall contain a water heater in safe and working condition.
(8) Egress windows. Each bedroom of a manufactured home shall have at least one operable window of sufficient size to allow egress if necessary.
(9) Ventilation. The kitchen in the home shall have at least one operating window or other ventilation device.
(10) Smoke detectors. Each pre-owned manufactured home shall contain one operable battery-powered smoke detector in each bedroom and in the kitchen, which must be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
(e) Enforcement.
(1) Permanent connection to utilities shall not be approved until the building inspector has issued a certificate of occupancy.
(2) Owners of pre-owned manufactured homes that are not in compliance upon a third inspection shall have their permit revoked and shall be required to remove the home from the jurisdiction at their own expense.
(3) The guarantee of condition bond or cash deposit will be forfeited after 90 days from the date of inspection, unless all conditions and standards are met prior to the end of the 90 days or an extension has been issued in writing by the building inspector.
(f) Penalties. Failure to remove a pre-owned manufactured home from the jurisdiction upon failure to receive a certificate of occupancy shall be punishable by a fine up to $1,000.00. Each day any violation under this section continues shall be considered a separate offense.

(a) Tents and temporary tensioned-membrane structures.
(1) All supporting members shall be of sufficient size and strength to support the structure.
(2) The poles and their supporting guys, stays, stakes, and fastenings shall be of sufficient strength and attachment to resist a minimum wind pressure of 20 lbf/ft (0.96 kPa) of projected area of the tent.
(3) Tents shall be adequately guyed, supported, and braced to withstand a minimum pressure or suction of 10 lbf/ft (0.48 kPa).
(4) Pull-down ropes (jump ropes) shall be provided on all poles.
(b) Air supported, air-inflated temporary membrane structures.
(1) Structural requirements.
a. Envelope design. The design, materials, and construction for the structural envelope shall conform to the requirements of this section. Membrane structures shall be designed by a licensed architect or engineer knowledgeable in this type of construction.
b. Material strength. Calculation of fabric stresses shall include consideration of inflation pressure; the radius of the structure; and wind, ice, snow and earthquake loads. The minimum design criteria for material strength shall comply with the requirements of ASI 77, Air Structures Design and Standards Manual. Minimum design criteria shall be for 80 mph (129 km/hr) wind conditions. More severe design loads, as specified in local building codes, shall be required as a result of local climatic conditions. All material characteristics shall be verified by an approved test method. Material strengths shall be certified by the manufacturer and verified by test date from an organization acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction.
c. Joint strength. All seams shall develop the full strength of the envelope material as specified in ASI 77, Air Structures Design and Standards Manual.
(2) Load distribution.
a. The envelope shall be patterned and constructed to minimize stress concentrations in crown areas, around openings, and where rigid components such as door frames, vent pipes, and structural members are attached to the envelope.
b. There shall be sufficient clearance between the envelope and rigid components to permit free movement under load.
c. Reinforced areas, such as around openings, shall provide a flexible but airtight seal.
(3) Pressurization (inflation) system.
a. The operating inflation pressure for the structure shall be adequate to withstand a wind velocity of 80 mph (129 km/hr). Pressurization for higher wind conditions shall be provided where required by local climatic conditions, as determined by local authorities.
b. The pressurization system shall consist of one or more operating blower units. The system shall include automatic control of auxiliary blower units to reliably maintain the required operating pressure. This equipment shall meet the following requirements:
1. Blowers shall be powered by continuous-rated motors at the maximum power required.
2. Blowers shall have adequate personnel protection, such as inlet screens and belt guards.
3. Blower systems shall be weather protected.
4. Blower systems shall be equipped with backdraft check dampers.
5. There shall be no fewer than two blower units, each of which has adequate capacity to maintain full inflation pressure with normal leakage.
6. The blowers shall be designed to be incapable of overpressurization.
7. The auxiliary blower unit(s) shall operate automatically if there is any loss of internal pressure or if an operating blower unit becomes inoperative.
8. The design inflation pressure and the capacity of each blower system shall be certified by a professional engineer.
(4) Standby power system.
a. Design. A fully automatic standby power system shall be provided. The system shall be either an auxiliary engine generator set capable of running the blower system or a supplementary blower unit that is sized for one times the normal operating capacity and is powered by an internal combustion engine.
b. The standby power system shall be fully automatic to ensure continuous inflation in the event of any failure of the primary power. This system shall be capable of operating continuously for a minimum of four hours.
c. Certification. The sizing and capacity of the standby power system shall be certified by a professional engineer.
(5) Anchorage design.
a. Basic requirements. A positive anchorage system shall be provided to securely anchor the envelope to the ground or to the structure.
b. Specific requirements. Anchor loading shall be determined and verified by analytical data prepared by a professional engineer. The minimum requirements for anchorage designs shall be in accordance with the requirements of ASI 77, Air Structures Design and Standards Manual.
c. Accessory equipment. The design and use of accessory equipment for heating, air conditioning, lighting, and similar functions shall conform to the requirements of Chapter 10 and to approved recognized standards.
(Ord. No. 407, § IV, 8-6-02)
